docTitle: Pail · Desktop app for S3-compatible storage
docDescription: Pail is a free, open-source desktop app for managing Amazon S3, MinIO, Cloudflare R2 and other S3-compatible storage on Windows, Linux and macOS.
heroSub: Browse and manage Amazon S3, MinIO, Cloudflare R2 and any other S3-compatible storage from one desktop app. Free and open source, for Windows, Linux and macOS.
shotAlt: The Pail main window: bucket list, object table and inspector
featuresTitle: Everything a bucket needs, in one window.
fTransfersBody: Uploads and downloads run in separate queues, with progress, speed, cancel and retry. Large files go up in parts with checksums, and a download reaches its destination only after it has been verified.
fPaletteBody: Press Ctrl+K (⌘K on macOS) to find any command, bucket or tool. English and Chinese keywords both work.
fSettingsTitle: 14 bucket settings, as forms or JSON
fSettingsBody: Versioning, encryption, policy, CORS, lifecycle, replication and more. If your provider does not support a setting, Pail says so instead of showing it as empty.
fVersionsBody: See every version of an object, restore an older one or undo a delete, and permanently remove only the versions you choose.
fSyncTitle: Sync that shows its plan first
fSyncBody: Upload, download or mirror a folder. Compare by size and time, size only, or checksum, and exclude files by pattern. Only the actions you previewed run, and local files Pail deletes go to the system trash.
fLinksBody: Create presigned GET or PUT links with an expiry, for one object or many. Set a CDN domain on an account and copy the CDN link as soon as an upload finishes.
fRulesBody: Rules matched by bucket and key pattern set headers, storage class and encryption on upload, and can compress files with GZIP, ZIP or AES-256 ZIP.
cliTitle: The same accounts, in your terminal.
cliBody: pail uses the same accounts and saved sync jobs as the desktop app. Add --json for machine-readable output. Exit codes are stable, and credentials are never printed.
pKeysBody: Secret keys are stored in Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain or the Linux Secret Service. Where there is no keychain, use the optional vault, encrypted with Argon2id and XChaCha20-Poly1305.
pNetBody: Pail talks only to the storage endpoints of the accounts you add, and to nothing else.
pLogBody: The diagnostic log stays off until you turn it on, and it strips signatures, Authorization headers, URL query strings and known secrets.
pScopeTitle: See the scope before you confirm
pScopeBody: Destructive actions list what they will affect before they run. To delete a bucket, you type its name.
dlgConfirm: Type the bucket name to confirm
osLinuxReq: A .tar.gz with pail-desktop, pail, a .desktop entry and an icon
osMacReq: A .zip with Pail.app and pail · macOS 11 or later
downloadNote: The archives are not code-signed. The macOS app is not notarized and has not been tested on a real Mac yet.
demoHint2: to try Pail against a built-in in-memory S3 server. Nothing leaves your computer.

docStartDesc: How to install Pail, add an account, use the command line and build from source, plus where Pail keeps your data and which platforms are tested.
